highlights.title: 只看得到结局的中介者，怎么把整场博弈掰向自己
highlights.title_en: Learning and Steering in Incomplete-Information Games
highlights.summary: In many modern multi-agent systems, a mediator seeks to influence strategic decision dynamics using only outcome-level feedback and without knowing agents' utilities. In this work, we study how a mediator can learn an unknown game and steer adaptive agents toward outcomes that maximize her utility using only trajectory feedback. The mediator knows the game form and her own objective, but not the agents' utilities. Moreover, she commits to nonnegative payments and provides recommendations and contexts, but receives only a single realized terminal outcome rather than full-information feedback. We develop halving-type algorithms that learn utility differences in normal-form games and conditional continuation-value differences in extensive-form games, achieving a sample complexity of $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ that matches worst-case lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. We then combine these learning procedures with a Lagrangian formulation in an online Learn-Compute-Steer algorithm that interleaves learning, equilibrium computation, and steering toward mediator-optimal extensive-form correlated equilibria (EFCE). With high probability, the Learn-Compute-Steer algorithm achieves a directness gap and an optimality gap of $\widetilde O(T^{-1/4})$, while time-average payments are of $\widetilde O(T^{-1/8})$.

highlights.glance: 只拿到一条终局轨迹，也能边学博弈边转向：学效用差的样本复杂度打到下界，转向缺口以四次方根速率收敛，而支付的时均量以八次方根消失

essay.v: 一个平台想让局面朝自己有利的方向走，却看不见参与者的偏好，每一轮只能看到最终成交的那一笔。这个信息落差决定了「学」和「控」不能分两步做：你必须在同一个循环里既摸清对方在乎什么，又把推荐和补贴发出去。这篇来自伊利诺伊大学的工作，把这件事在扩展形博弈里做到了有收敛速率。
先把「谁知道什么」交代清楚
设定是这样的：中介者知道博弈的形式，也知道自己的目标函数，唯独不知道各方的效用。她可以承诺非负的支付，可以向各方发放推荐与上下文，但每一轮只收到一条实际走到的终局路径，而不是完整的收益向量。对方的策略也不是某个固定均衡，而是无遗憾学习者的在线轨迹。
这个设定与贝叶斯说服、机制设计的老文献有个关键差别：说服理论里接收方的策略是静态的最优反应，机制设计里参与者的类型分布是给定的；这里两者都不是，参与者会随反馈调整，而中介者要在这种适应过程中保持掌控。作者把反馈粒度当成全文的分水岭——全信息反馈下可以评估未发生的偏离，轨迹反馈下只能从一条路径上反推反事实，而后者才是平台、监管者、竞价系统的真实处境。
减半法：从一条路径里榨出效用差
技术支点是减半类算法。在正规形博弈里学各方两两之间的效用差；在扩展形博弈里学的是「条件延续值差」——给定某个信息集确实被到达时，从这里继续走下去的价值差。
这一步选择很讲究：扩展形相关均衡的激励约束恰好只依赖条件延续值差，而不需要完整效用。于是学到它，就等于拿到了评估均衡可实施性的全部素材，不必去复原整张收益表。样本复杂度是 ε 的负二次方量级（差一个对数因子），与已知的最坏情况下界对齐；对扩展形，作者还自己给出一条下界命题，把上界钉住。
与最接近的前作相比，这里修了两处：一是把结论从正规形推到扩展形，二是把对动作空间规模的依赖收紧——原来的界在动作数很大时实际上不可用。
学、算、转，三件事缠在一个循环里
光会学不够。中介者还得在线算均衡并施加影响，于是有了「学—算—转」框架：用拉格朗日化把「转向对中介者最优的扩展形相关均衡」写成带约束的在线问题，每一轮交替做三件事——更新对效用差的估计、重算当前的扩展形相关均衡、按这个均衡向各方发推荐与支付。
收敛刻画分三层。相对最优值的直接性缺口与最优性缺口都按轮数四分之一次方的倒数量级收敛；而时均支付按八分之一次方的倒数消失。两个速率不同，含义很实在：钱最终不用花，但花得比缺口收敛慢一档，因为早期为换取服从所付的补偿支付被稀释得更慢。三条结论都是高概率成立，不是期望意义。
实验只有两个小例子，但看得很准
正规形用猎鹿博弈，中介者最大化归一化社会福利，最优点本身就是一个严格纳什均衡，几乎没有「目标与可行性冲突」的干扰，适合验证机制本身是否跑得动。扩展形用两人库恩扑克，十次独立运行，看前五万轮。三条曲线在初始瞬态之后同步下降，与定理给出的速率方向一致。
猎鹿实验里能看到两个时间尺度的分离：服从在第一轮更新之后就建立起来（补偿支付随即塌陷），而推荐分布的改进要慢得多。轨迹图上，十个分层的初始点先被拉向推荐分布，再沿对角线走向最优结局——作者用这个图把「先学会听话」和「再学会指路」两个阶段拆开，比单看收敛曲线清楚。
怎么读这篇
这是预印本，贡献在理论侧，实验规模很小：两个玩具博弈、二十与十个随机种子，没有真实平台数据，也没有和既有转向算法的同条件对照。两个假设要特别留意：第一，各方在每个由中介者给定的上下文内都是无遗憾的，一旦推荐变化过于频繁，这个假设就不成立；第二，中介者知道博弈形式，只不知道效用——若形式本身也要学，界会退化。文中致谢明确写了用大模型辅助证明与实验，定理陈述仍建议自行复核。
可迁移的启发：在形式化「影响一个会学习的人」之前，先问自己拿到的反馈粒度是什么。如果只有终局，那么所有反事实都得靠主动扰动去换，而补贴的消失速率会稳定地比策略的收敛速率慢一档——这个时间差就是预算规划的真实约束，不是实现细节。

highlights.title: 二十三年后重开知识平面：让互不信任的网络智能体坐到一起
highlights.summary: In 2003, Clark et al. proposed the "Knowledge Plane", a layer of intelligent agents that share rich information about network state in order to collaboratively manage the Internet across administrative boundaries. The technology of the day lacked the two capabilities it demanded most: reasoning and unstructured communication. Thus, automated network management has remained largely confined to single domains, while interdomain problems are still resolved by human operators on the phone. We argue that agentic large language models can finally unlock the potential of the Knowledge Plane, but that doing so will require solving new research problems that arise particularly in this decentralized, multi-agent, coopetitive setting that have received limited attention in the literature thus far.
highlights.summary_short: In 2003, Clark et al. proposed the "Knowledge Plane", a layer of intelligent agents that share rich information about network state in order to collaboratively manage the Internet across administrative boundaries.
highlights.section: LLM 多智能体与社会模拟
highlights.glance: 2003 年的「知识平面」构想缺的两样东西今天都有了，作者用四个模型在虚拟网络上跑通排障、劫持与按合同选路，然后指出真正的难点是互不信任的谈判

essay.v: 一个学生打不开某个网站。原因可能在校园防火墙、上游路由、域名解析，也可能在对端服务器过载。要定位它，需要横跨四五个互不隶属的网络去取数据——而现实中这通电话要打几个小时，且只有大厂打得通。二十三年前有人提议给互联网加一层「知识平面」，让各家网络各派一个智能体交换状态、协作排障。当时的机器缺两样东西：推理，和非结构化通信。今天这两样恰好都有了。
为什么是自然语言，而不是又一套协议
作者给出的理由不是「大模型很强」，而是协议本身的固有问题。跨自治系统交换遥测需要先定义格式，格式一旦定下就迅速僵化：一家的新技术，另一家还没跟上，字段就编不进去。自然语言是前后兼容的——发送方可以直接解释「这个新指标是什么意思」。第二层理由更实际：运营商有隐私顾虑，不愿意无条件共享遥测，而「哪些数据是解决当前问题所必需的」是个推理问题，静态访问控制列表回答不了。
代价也在这里。协议免费提供了身份、授权、审计，语言一样都不给。所以论文后半段几乎全在讨论「对方凭什么信你」。
六条要求，前三条已经做到了
作者从原始论文里抽出六条要求：把高层目标拆成低层动作、从历史动作中学习、在通用性下工作、跨网络合并视角、在信息不完整甚至恶意时仍能工作、在各方目标冲突时仍能工作。前三条只考单智能体能力，现有工作（包括某头部公司的生产级工具）基本都满足了；后三条才是多域的真问题，而它们恰恰是文献空白——这个切分是全文最有价值的判断。
三个仿真实例
实验在虚拟网络环境里搭：每个主机一个智能体，只能操作自己的主机、只知道邻居，没有任何全局视角。四个模型参赛，两个闭源旗舰加两个开源权重模型。智能体通过独立于数据面的消息通道通信，每次调用工具都必须写一段自由文本理由——这些理由后来成了论文里信息量最大的引文。
第一个场景复现原始论文的例子，三种成因：校园防火墙误拦、上游域名解析过期、对端服务器被打满。多数模型能逐级升级、定位根因，并且在「需要管理员批准」这条边界上停手；也有模型把域名问题读成路由问题，还有模型把正常请求误判成慢速攻击并把对方地址公开出去——后者恰好说明「隐私指令」与「排障效率」会正面冲突。
第二个场景是 2022 年某跨链桥的边界网关劫持：攻击者用小运营商宣告一段云厂商地址，且这条宣告能通过路由源验证。一个模型把「验证通过」当成足够证据装了进去；其余模型抓住三处破绽——注册库条目未被验证、小运营商不可能直连并转接云厂商流量、以及云厂商智能体否认授权过那条记录。这里的说服力不在单点校验，而在交叉质询：它把「不可信的一方可能在撒谎」变成了可执行的验证步骤。
第三个场景最有意思：不再用边界网关协议，让智能体直接按合同选路。一个运营商接两家上游，便宜的一美元每兆，贵的五美元每兆且按三十天计费周期的高分位计费。智能体学会了把每天几小时的流量尖峰甩给贵的那家——因为最忙的一成样本不进军费——然后在尖峰拖得太久、丢弃额度快用完时切回便宜的那家。这种「读合同条款做决策」的行为，固定协议做不到，因为它把百分比计费这件事写死在配置里，而智能体是每轮重新算一遍。
真正的难点是互不信任的协作
作者把挑战分两类。通用的一类是成本与可控性：现架构下每个实体都要调一个大模型，互联网规模下不可承受，可行路径是粗粒度部署（一个自治系统一个）、模型级联、开源权重自托管。另一类是这一场景独有的：选择性信息披露，以及互不信任的智能体之间的协作。
作者把后者称为「去中心化谈判」，并指出机器学习文献几乎没有对应的问题设定：机器人集群是为了共同目标，而这里的各方目标可能相互冲突、彼此不公开。要推进它，第一步不是算法，而是指标与基准——这句话说得客气，实际是在说这个方向还没有可比的评价体系。
怎么读这篇
这是热网研讨会的立场论文（已录用，附正式出版信息与数字对象标识），不是完整系统论文。三个案例都是小规模仿真，没有规模化部署、没有成本测量、没有对抗性红队测试；四个模型的对比是「能/不能」的定性观察，每种配置的重复次数很少，无法给出统计结论。作者也明确选择了暂时搁置「该不该让智能体管互联网」，只做「如果这么做会遇到什么」的思想实验——读的时候要守住这条边界，别把它当成部署建议。
可迁移的启发：当一个系统由互不信任、目标不一致的自治方组成时，通用自然语言往往比精细协议更容易起步，因为协议需要共识，语言只需要解释。但你必须自己补上协议免费提供的东西——身份、授权、审计，以及「对方在撒谎」这件事的处理流程。补不上，这套东西就只能停在仿真里。

radar.title: The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
radar.summary: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type–specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

radar.title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
radar.summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re 2 Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

radar.title: Robust Auction Design with Support Information
radar.summary: A seller wants to sell an item to n buyers. Buyer valuations are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) according to a distribution unknown to the seller; the seller only knows that the support is included in [a, b]. To be robust, the seller chooses a dominant strategy incentive compatible mechanism that optimizes the worst-case performance relative to the ideal expected revenue the seller could have collected with knowledge of buyers’ valuations. Our analysis unifies the regret and the ratio objectives. For these objectives, we derive an optimal mechanism and the corresponding performance in quasi-closed form, as a function of the support information [a, b] and the number of buyers n. Our analysis reveals three regimes of support information and a new class of robust mechanisms. (i) When a/b is below a threshold, the optimal mechanism is a second-price auction (SPA) with random reserve, a focal class in earlier literature. (ii) When a/b is above another threshold, SPAs are strictly suboptimal, and an optimal mechanism belongs to a class of mechanisms we introduce, which we call pooling auctions (POOL); whenever the highest value is above a threshold, the mechanism still allocates to the highest bidder, but otherwise the mechanism allocates to a uniformly random buyer, that is, pools low types. (iii) When a/b is between two thresholds, a randomization between SPA and POOL is optimal. We also characterize optimal mechanisms within nested central subclasses of mechanisms: standard mechanisms that only allocate to the highest bidder, SPA with random reserve, and SPA with no reserve. We show strict separations in terms of performance across classes, implying that deviating from standard mechanisms is necessary for robustness. Lastly, we show that the same results hold under other distribution classes that capture “positive dependence,” namely i.i.d., mixture of i.i.d., and exchangeable and affiliated distributions, as well as i.i.d. regular distributions. This paper was accepted by David Simchi-Levi, revenue management and market analytics. Supplemental Material: The online appendices are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.02703 .

radar.title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability
radar.summary: Abstract Knowledge-constrained network inference enables the reconstruction of regulatory programmes from high-dimensional biological data, yet the conditions under which shared and context-specific structures can be reliably identified remain poorly understood. Pablo Rodriguez-Mier et al. recently introduced CORNETO, a framework for multi-sample constrained inference. Here we reproduce, evaluate and extend CORNETO in terms of robustness, identifiability and bias–variance trade-offs. Using dynamic haematopoiesis and stable cortical datasets, we systematically assess four network reconstruction paradigms while preserving the original method-specific evaluation procedures and benchmark definitions. We show that multi-sample inference generally improves robustness and reproducibility, although gains in predictive performance depend on biological context and the completeness of the prior network. To enhance stability, we introduce bootstrap aggregation and selective re-expansion strategies that improve consensus robustness and recovery while preserving context-specific signals without modifying the underlying optimization scheme or sacrificing generality. Across datasets and methods, our results reveal distinct inference regimes governed by sample availability, prior knowledge and regularization. Together, these findings position network reconstruction as a regime-dependent learning problem and provide practical principles for robust multi-sample biological network inference.

radar.title: Cooling fast and slow: Characterizing the effects of vitrification in cryo-EM and the subsequent recovery of equilibrium populations
radar.venue_raw: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
radar.summary: Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), a powerful class of techniques in structural biology with the potential to resolve molecular ensembles, requires that samples be vitrified to protect them from the high vacuum of the electron microscope. However, the effects of vitrification on biomolecular ensembles are unknown. To study them, we carried out extensive molecular dynamics simulations (over 50 ms) of the Trp-cage miniprotein at equilibrium and undergoing rapid cooling. We simulated seven cooling rates spanning three orders of magnitude, with the slowest coolings matching experimental rates. By inspecting molecular mobility and density-temperature trajectories for water with and without protein, we found that water vitrification is unaltered by the protein. To track protein conformation changes, and to relate them to kinetics, we made a Markov State Model (MSM) of Trp-cage from 5.4 ms of equilibrium sampling at 277 K. We observed that MSM states with a characteristic time longer than the duration of the nonequilibrium cooling tend to be more robust to artifacts induced by such cooling. Critically, although we observe that some states vanish in the equilibrium ensemble at 230 K, none do in our nonequilibrium cooled ensembles. To account for these perturbations, we developed a thermodynamic inference framework for recovering equilibrium populations from vitrified ensembles. These results indicate that cryo-EM has the capacity to be an accurate technique for the study of biomolecular ensembles.

radar.title: Agentic AI system for hospital management
radar.summary: Abstract In modern-day hospital administration, there are many problems like long waiting time for patients, poor scheduling of physicians, lack of coordination between departments, among others. As such, this research suggests an Agentic AI System for Hospital Administration that utilizes a multi agent architecture and intelligence embedding to automate healthcare processes. This model entails a Patient Interaction Agent, a Care Coordination Agent, a Doctor Interaction Agent, and a Bed Allocation Agent, whose main roles are facilitating patients' entry and sorting out the patients' needs, allocation of doctors to attend to patients, coordination within the hospital, and hospital resource management, respectively.Through reinforcement learning, decision-making based on information processing, and synchronization, the framework becomes more adaptive and scalable. It is expected that due to intelligence distribution and intelligent decision-making, this model will minimize total waiting time, improve physicians' usage, and enhance scheduling of patients. Empirical analysis shows that hospital operations exhibit significant performance superiority of agentic models over the traditional models.Modern hospital administration faces major challenges such as prolonged patient waiting times, inefficient physician scheduling, poor interdepartmental coordination, and suboptimal resource utilization. Traditional hospital management systems often rely on static and centralized approaches that lack adaptability in dynamic healthcare environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL)-based intelligent hospital administration framework for workflow optimization and resource management. The proposed system consists of four collaborative agents: a Patient Interaction Agent for patient triage, a Doctor Scheduling Agent for dynamic physician allocation, a Care Coordination Agent for interdepartmental communication, and a Bed Allocation Agent for adaptive resource management. The agents utilize decentralized decision-making and reinforcement learning to optimize hospital operations in real time. The framework is evaluated using a hospital simulation environment and compared with conventional scheduling and management approaches. The results show that the effectiveness of the proposed system model is able to complete the tasks at a rate of 82.50\% in a period of 5.12 seconds with a success rate in handling queries of 79.15\%. Furthermore, the system attains a coordination efficiency of 87.50\%, indicating effective collaboration among agents, while maintaining an agent conflict rate of 5.00\%, ensuring stable and interference-free operations. The framework records a low communication overhead of 0.88, reflecting efficient inter-agent communication, and achieves a convergence rate of 96.4\%, demonstrating learning stability and adaptability.This indicates that the model is efficient, scalable, and adaptable in managing intelligent hospitals.

radar.title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD+ hydrolysis
radar.summary: Abstract The Kongming (Kom) system, consisting of KomA, KomB, and KomC, protects bacteria from phage infection. KomA collaborates with a phage enzyme to generate deoxyinosine 5′-triphosphate (dITP), which activates the KomBC complex to hydrolyze NAD⁺ and trigger cell death. Recent studies propose that dITP activates KomBC through a simple conformational change. Our findings instead reveal a more dynamic mechanism. Without dITP, KomBC complexes exist in equilibrium between tightly packed oligomers and loosely packed filaments, both inactive. Tight packing accumulates unfavorable electrostatic interactions without positioning catalytic residues for NAD⁺ hydrolysis, whereas loose packing relieves these interactions but leaves catalytic residues misaligned. dITP binding at KomB stabilizes tightly packed KomC cores in the filament while aligning catalytic residues. Therefore, a small-molecule signal activates signaling by shifting the assembly equilibrium of higher-order protein complexes toward a catalytically competent state.

Recursive Adversarial Engine: A Stability-Oriented Architecture for Reliable Large Language Model Multi-Agent Systems
radar.venue: International Journal of Advanced AI Applications
radar.venue_raw: International Journal of Advanced AI Applications
radar.summary: Large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems are rapidly migrating from laboratory prototypes to production deployments in finance, scientific research, industrial digital twins, and urban scheduling. As deployment scales, however, a family of systemic pathologies persists: decision oscillation driven by zero-sum agent interactions, cascade propagation of hallucinated content, long-horizon behavioral drift, value misalignment, and unresolved inter-agent conflict. Existing orchestration paradigms, which rely on instruction dispatch, greedy optimization, or static rules, address only shallow coordination and provide no principled mechanism for convergence. This paper proposes the Recursive Adversarial Engine (RAE), a runtime architecture for multi-agent systems organized around three propositions: bounded adversarial interaction supplies the error-detection signal, recursive correction supplies the error-elimination mechanism, and dynamic checks and balances supply the stability guarantee. We specify a four-layer reference architecture comprising adversarial verification, recursive correction, checks-and-balances scheduling, and steady-state output, and we characterize its convergence behavior through a Lyapunov-style stability argument. A qualitative comparison with self-play, multi-agent debate, alignment, and consensus frameworks delineates the paradigm difference. Engineering implications for high-stakes domains, long-horizon robustness, auditability, and middleware integration are analyzed, and open challenges are identified.

radar.title: Public Signals in Affine Network Congestion Games with Uncertain Free-Flow Times
radar.summary: Travel times in road networks are subject to stochastic uncertainty resulting from various parameters. A benevolent mobility service provider observing the actual travel times from data may use its informational advantage to steer the traffic equilibrium in a favorable direction through a processs known as signaling or Bayesian persuasion. Previous work has shown that the underlying signaling problem can be NP-hard to approximate better than [Formula: see text], even for static Wardrop flows with affine cost functions with stochastic offsets. In contrast, we show that in this case, the signaling problem is easy for many networks. First, we tightly characterize the class of single-commodity networks in which full information revelation is always an optimal signaling strategy. Second, we construct a reduction from optimal signaling to computing an optimal collection of active edges for the Wardrop equilibrium. For two states, this allows us to efficiently compute an optimal signaling scheme whenever the number of different active edge sets is bounded by a polynomial in the input size. Using a cell decomposition technique, we extend the approach to a polynomial-time algorithm for multicommodity parallel-edge networks provided that both the number of commodities and states are constant. radar.title: Strategic ignorance and information design
radar.summary: We study information design in strategic settings when agents can publicly refuse to view their private signals. Ignoring the constraints that agents must be willing to view their signals may lead to substantial divergence between the designer’s intent and actual outcomes, even in the case where the designer seeks to maximize the agents’ payoffs. We introduce the appropriate equilibrium concept — ignorance-permissive Bayes correlated equilibrium — and characterize implementable distributions over states and actions. The designer’s optimal response to strategic ignorance generates qualitative properties that standard information design cannot: the designer may provide redundant or even counterproductive information, asymmetric information structures may be strictly optimal in symmetric environments, providing information conditional on players’ viewing choices rather than all at once may hurt the designer, and communication between players may help her. Optimality sometimes requires that players ignore their signals with positive probability.

radar.title: Multiagent Assortment Optimization in Sequential Matching Markets
radar.summary: Motivated by the challenges faced by choice-based matching platforms, in this work, we study a generalization of the two-sided assortment optimization model. Specifically, this model consists of two sides (e.g., customers and suppliers) who have preferences over the opposite side in the form of discrete choice models. A matching is realized through a two-step process where the platform’s decision is to initially present to each agent on one side an assortment of users of the opposite side. The ultimate goal of the platform is to maximize the total expected revenue collected from the matching. Because of the computational complexity of this problem, we focus on the design of approximation algorithms with constant-factor guarantees for the constrained version of the problem under general choice preferences. First, to the best of our knowledge, we are the first to draw connections with the literature of submodular optimization and show that one-sided choice-oblivious approaches perform arbitrarily badly. Second, we show that, for the general setting, there exists a two-sided choice-aware randomized algorithm that achieves a [Formula: see text]-approximation factor, which is the best possible. Third, we design an algorithm that is asymptotically optimal when one side follows the well-known multinomial logit (MNL) choice model under the small probability regime. Fourth, we provide a simple and effective algorithm with a [Formula: see text]-approximation guarantee for the unconstrained setting, with both sides following MNL models. Finally, we assess the performance of our proposed methods with a detailed computational study and discuss several extensions. Funding: M. radar.title: Multi-AI agent framework reveals the “oxide gatekeeper” in aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
radar.venue_raw: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
radar.summary: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic “gatekeeper,” regulating oxidation through a “breathing mode” of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a “rupture mode” leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.

Implementation via political parties
radar.summary: We address the implementation of public policies (alternatives) when the feasible set is unknown to the planner. The implementing agents are the political parties, who know the feasible set. They care about the implemented alternative, which reflects their ideology, and their share in parliament and office. They face a mechanism that, given the alternatives proposed by all parties, asks the voters to rank them and determines the chosen alternative and the shares in parliament and office. We identify conditions on parties’ preferences that guarantee the socially optimal policy is the outcome of the unique pure strategy Nash equilibrium of the electoral game played by the parties. The existence of the equilibrium does not require any assumptions about the parties’ ideology. To ensure uniqueness, shares must prevail over ideology: office or parliamentary shares in two-party systems, and strictly office shares in systems with more than two parties.

radar.title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
radar.summary: Abstract Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

radar.title: Multitype Information Acquisition in a Strategic Trading Model
radar.summary: We analyze information acquisition in a strategic trading model with multidimensional uncertainties. Our main result is that the equilibrium can exhibit multiplicity because of the integer nature of the number of informed traders and the strategic interactions across different types of informed traders. We show that the number of equilibria can be arbitrarily large. Moreover, asymmetric equilibria can arise even in symmetric settings. As information costs rise, fewer traders acquire information, yet prices can become more informative. These results shed light on the instability of financial markets and yield testable empirical predictions. This paper was accepted by Lukas Schmid, finance. radar.title: Contest or Contract: Assessing the Effectiveness of Contests in Online Labor Markets
radar.summary: Online labor markets have become increasingly popular among companies seeking global access to workers. Some platforms have adopted a contest-based scheme, allowing employers to review multiple submissions before selecting the best one. This practice raises a crucial question: Given a predefined budget, should employers choose a contest or contract scheme for tasks? This study examines the comparative effectiveness of contests versus contracts in achieving better job outcomes, focusing on design tasks characterized by high uncertainty. Using a comprehensive data set from a leading online labor market, we employ multiple empirical strategies, combined with machine learning and text mining techniques, to examine the impact of compensation schemes on job quality. Our results suggest that contract-based jobs yield better performance than contests in the context of ideation tasks. Further analysis, such as examining image similarity among pairwise solutions within a task, identifies “copying” behaviors as a key mechanism undermining the effectiveness of contests. In the public setting of contests, workers can observe others’ submissions and revise their own, leading to imitation rather than innovation. As competition intensity increases, workers have weaker incentives to exert effort, reducing solution quality. Consequently, the negative incentive effects in contests outweigh both the potential positive incentive and parallel effects. Moreover, although information availability can enhance work quality, contests inherently offer limited informational advantages compared with contracts. Taken together, our findings suggest that contract-based schemes are more effective than contests for design tasks, offering important implications for both employers and platform designers in online labor markets. radar.title: Nash Equilibrium-Driven Adaptive Behavior in Swarm Intelligence with Self-Organizing Maps
radar.summary: This paper proposes a swarm intelligence model that employs classical boid flocking dynamics combined with non-cooperative game-theoretic methods, specifically Nash Equilibrium, to simulate adaptive decision-making in multi-agent systems. The work leverages a payoff matrix based on fundamental flocking behaviors: cohesion, alignment, and separation, to enable each agent to dynamically optimize its own strategy based on local interactions within the group. The simulation introduces Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) for clustering and behavior adaptation, providing a machine learning perspective on agent categorization and role differentiation. To simulate real-world unpredictability, stochastic noise is used to understand how varying noise levels influence collective alignment and coherence. The results demonstrate the impact of environmental factors on emergent swarm behavior and showcase the benefits of combining machine learning and game theory for adaptive control in distributed systems. This work provides valuable insights into the interplay between noise, decision-making, and flocking dynamics, with broader applications in robotics, swarm intelligence, and autonomous systems.

SEER: A Scalable Event-Driven Runtime for Parallel Execution of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Environments
radar.summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is increasingly used in systems where many entities interact in a shared environment. In these workloads, policy inference can be batched on GPUs, but the CPU-side environment path still updates entity states, resolves local interactions, and builds observations inside each $\mathrm{env.step}$. This path can dominate latency in interaction-intensive workloads after policy batching. Existing vectorized environment interfaces and general event-driven runtimes do not directly address the fine-grained cross-entity work inside one bounded MARL step while preserving the step-level semantics expected by learning systems. We present SEER (Scalable Event-Driven Environment Runtime), a runtime for MARL environment execution under an explicit event-locality contract. SEER models each environment step as a bounded stream of timestamped events. If direct state updates are entity-local and cross-entity effects are represented as ordered future events, SEER can run independent events in parallel while preserving serial-equivalent boundary outputs. To make this contract practical, SEER uses a CAS-based dual-layer event queue: local event queues preserve per-entity causal order, while a parallel executive list exposes ready work to global worker threads. SEER further uses STPA, a preflight-guided thread-pool selection mechanism that combines short runtime traces with static workload and hardware features. We evaluate SEER on two parameterized MARL workloads: compute-intensive UAV swarm control (Aircraft) and communication-intensive wireless management (PCS). On Aircraft, SEER reduces inference latency by 16.2\% over the baseline. On PCS, SEER reduces environment-execution latency by 46.9\%, 19.5\%, and 64.9\% over ROSS-T, NBSE, and ROOT-Sim, respectively.

radar.title: On the Maximization of Long-Run Conditional Value-at-Risk for Markov Decision Processes
radar.summary: Optimizing Risk-Seeking Sequential Decisions via Conditional Value-at-Risk Decision makers may exhibit risk-seeking preferences in finance, energy operations, and stochastic resource management, yet corresponding Markov decision process (MDP) theories remain underdeveloped. In this paper, “On the Maximization of Long-Run CVaR for Markov Decision Processes,” Xia, Yu, and Wu investigate infinite-horizon MDPs maximizing long-run conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) for instantaneous rewards. They prove optimality for stationary randomized policies and show deterministic policies may fail; an optimal policy randomizes over at most two actions. By converting the original problem into a minimax saddle point formulation, the authors develop solvable linear programming and globally convergent gradient descent algorithms. Results are further extended to joint mean-CVaR optimization and validated on real-world microgrid scheduling data. This work fills gaps for risk-seeking MDPs and delivers practical computation tools for tail-oriented sequential decision making.

radar.title: Bargaining and Contract Forms in Distribution Channels: Why Do Slotting Fees Arise and Linear Contracts Persist?
radar.summary: Two empirical patterns emerge in business-to-business settings, particularly in retail distribution channels such as grocery markets. First, linear contracts are widely observed alongside nonlinear contracts with fixed payments, despite the claimed efficiency advantages of the latter. Second, when fixed payments arise, they often flow from suppliers to retailers (slotting fees) rather than the reverse. We develop and analyze a model of multilateral bargaining in which a supplier negotiates separately with competing retailers to explain these patterns. The key mechanism is a trade-off between two distortions: under linear contracts, wholesale prices reflect bargaining power and can be either above or below the channel-profit-maximizing level, whereas under two-part tariffs, wholesale prices are set to maximize bilateral surplus independently of bargaining power but are systematically too low from an overall channel perspective because of rent shifting across relationships. As a result, neither contractual form uniformly dominates; instead, relative performance depends on how bargaining shapes gains from trade across firms. When bargaining leads to slotting fees, two-part tariffs yield higher channel profits than linear contracts, whereas when it would imply payments from retailers to suppliers, linear contracts may perform better. These findings offer a unified explanation for the persistence of linear contracts alongside two-part tariffs, the direction of fixed payments, and the conditions under which each contractual form is likely to arise. This paper was accepted by Miguel Villas-Boas, marketing. Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.03426 .

radar.title: Autonomous biomedical research with an artificial intelligence agent
radar.summary: Biomedical research is increasingly constrained by repetitive, fragmented workflows that slow discovery. We introduce Biomni, a general-purpose biomedical artificial intelligence agent that autonomously executes diverse research tasks. To map the biomedical action space, Biomni’s action-discovery agent mines tools, databases, and protocols from thousands of publications across 25 domains, building a unified agentic environment. Its general-purpose architecture integrates large language model reasoning with retrieval-augmented planning and code-based execution, dynamically composing workflows without predefined templates. Systematic benchmarking shows strong generalization across heterogeneous tasks—causal gene prioritization, drug repurposing, rare-disease diagnosis, microbiome analysis, and molecular cloning—without task-specific tuning. Real-world case studies demonstrate Biomni interpreting multimodal datasets, optimizing protein stability, orchestrating wet-lab instruments, and generating experimentally testable protocols. Biomni envisions artificial intelligence augmenting human scientists and accelerating discovery.

radar.title: Cyber Defence, Agentic AI, and the Sociotechnical Paradigm: A Survey of AI-Driven Cybersecurity
radar.venue: International Journal of Applied Smart Interdisciplinary Technologies
radar.venue_raw: International Journal of Applied Smart Interdisciplinary Technologies
radar.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping cybersecurity, moving it from signature-based reactive security to agentic, self-evolving, and proactive operations. However, the fast deployment of autonomous agents entails significant security issues, physical-layer attacks in cyber-physical systems, alignment problems, and advanced social engineering risks jeopardizing the stability of the modern sociotechnical infrastructures. This survey paper, which summarizes and analyses the literature, examines the duality of AI in cybersecurity, exploring its implications for strengthening digital defences and increasing the threat landscape for adversaries. We perform a thorough review of 36 cutting-edge research articles, which are organized into six important areas: self-evolving defensive paradigms, LLM-based intelligent agents, reinforcement learning for autonomous decision-making, security of cyber-physical systems, human-machine co-teaming, and agent alignment. Our synthesis shows that multi-agent collaborations greatly shorten incident response times and automate discovery of vulnerabilities but are also highly vulnerable to prompt injection, training data poisoning, and physical-layer spoofing. Moreover, we identify a shift from model patches to model alignment and constitutional safety at runtime as a prerequisite for securing these systems. We believe that resilient digital defence must also be considered a sociotechnical problem, as there must be agents, autonomous systems, that are governed by other agents, aligned and constitutionally bound, and are able to collaborate, rather than operate completely separately, with human operators.

radar.title: Research on Simulation and Path Optimization of University Emergency Evacuation Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
radar.summary: To address the spatial misalignment between local observations and global bottleneck consequences in university emergency evacuation, as well as the difficulty of sparse team rewards in guiding diversion behaviors, the Topological Awareness Hierarchical State Encoder (TAHSE) and Bottleneck Sensitive Reward Decomposition Mechanism (BSRD) are proposed. These two mechanisms are coupled into a unified architecture within a centralized training-decentralized execution framework. TAHSE aggregates the features of the local neighborhood graph using attention and uses learnable bottleneck tokens as the keys and values for the second layer's cross-domain attention, enabling agents to obtain the compressed prior of the global bottleneck solely based on their own observations and pre-stored bottleneck graphs, reducing the computational complexity from the square level of the full graph attention to the linear level. BSRD decomposes a single negative time team reward into three components: progress, bottleneck pressure, and coordination completion. It triggers pressure penalties with a warning threshold lower than the safety upper limit and uses an adaptive coefficient to weigh the safety constraints as the difficulty of the scenario increases. Twenty seed repetition experiments were conducted in three-tier campus scenarios (500/1500/3000 agents) and structured perturbation protocols: The gap ratio of the proposed method relative to the upper bound reference in the three scenarios was controlled within 15%, while the MAPPO baseline increased from 18.4% to 31.5% as the scale expanded; the peak density effect under topological perturbation reached 1.42 (p<0.001), and the triggering threshold for diversion shifted systematically towards the bottleneck nodes with reduced capacity. The results show that embedding the bottleneck as a portable prior in the decentralized strategy and guiding diversion with reward signals ahead of the safety upper limit can achieve joint improvement in efficiency and safety at a controllable computational cost and is more reliable under structural variation conditions.

radar.title: Community-Oriented Market Design for Nonprofit Resource Exchange
radar.summary: Unlocking Value Through Nonprofit Resource Sharing Nonprofit organizations often operate under tight budgets while idle equipment, unused space, and shareable skills and expertise are frequently underutilized, with existing resource exchanges in the nonprofit sector limited to bilateral barter or relatively homogeneous resources. In “Community-Oriented Market Design for Nonprofit Resource Exchange,” Huang et al. propose Sharing With a Purpose (SWAP), a resource-sharing system that enables nonprofits to exchange heterogeneous resources without monetary payments. SWAP combines an auction-based process, SWAPcredit valuation, and integer optimization to facilitate multilateral exchanges, allowing nonprofits to obtain needed resources by contributing resources of their own. The authors implement this market design through the SWAP Hub, a digital platform deployed with nonprofit communities in multiple regions. Through repeated exchange episodes, participating organizations have shared not only physical assets but also a wide range of skills, services, and expertise, including marketing, management, event planning, and organizational development. The study demonstrates how innovative market design can unlock latent value in community resources, alleviate resource constraints, and encourage new connections and collaboration among nonprofit organizations.

radar.title: UNIHAA: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Autonomous Healthcare Appointment Management – From Behavioral Theory to Agentic Action
radar.summary: Background: No shows are a loss of clinical time, add to waiting lists and break continuity of care. The literature review indicates that the prediction of no-shows is still a significant challenge and reminder and targeted-intervention strategies have been shown to decrease no-shows, but with varying effects depending on the context [25-27]. The new healthcare literature also recognizes agentic and multi-agent AI as the new strategies of coordinated and goal-oriented workflows [1,5]. The aim of UNIHAA was to transcend the passive risk prediction, and to work towards coordinated, transparent and safety-governed action.Methods: We analysed 3,275,731 eligible non-cancelled outpatient visits of Saudi military healthcare facilities in 2021-2025; three records with missing covariate data were not included in the multivariable regression analysis, resulting in N=3,275,728. The empirical analysis looked at the trends of time, the impact of lead time, the variation of facilities and specialties, and history-conscious forecasting. UNIHAA combines the Individual, Clinical, System and Environmental levels of the Integrated Behavioral Access Network (IBAN) with a 10-agent architecture. It consists of history-sensitive risk stratification, LinUCB contextual-bandit intervention selection, dynamic slot recovery, federated multi-site learning, Page-Hinkley concept-drift detection, PPO-based coordination with Centralized Training Decentralized Execution (CTDE), FHIR interoperability, explainable AI, and human oversight.Results: The overall no-show rate in the retrospective study was 22.6% and the historical rate of no-show has decreased from 30.2% in 2021 to 18.7% in 2025. There was a strong association between extended lead times ( >60 days) and non-attendance (adjusted OR 2.47, 95% CI 2.44-2.51). The administrative-only model had an AUC of 0.605, on the complete data set. The development AUC=0.790 (95% CI 0.789-0.791), temporal holdout AUC=0.782, Brier score=0.171, PR-AUC=0.523 and ECE=0.018 were obtained in the companion AALAM analysis of a separate history-eligible cohort (N=672,441). Due to the different cohorts used for evaluation, the AUCs of the two models are descriptive benchmarks and not a same-cohort effect estimate. An assumption-based LinUCB policy simulation projected a 4.2 percentage-point attendance uplift (28,243 additional attended appointments over two years in the modeled cohort), while dynamic overbooking simulation recovered 12.3% of otherwise lost capacity. Federated prediction achieved AUC=0.785 versus 0.790 under centralized pooled training.Conclusions: UNIHAA extends the previously published AALAM empirical study through an original, theory-informed architecture for AI-driven healthcare appointment decisions. Its proposed contributions include hierarchical multi-agent coordination, contextual-bandit intervention selection, reinforcement-learning-based operational optimization, fairness-constrained decision governance, and human oversight. Retrospective predictive findings and simulation-derived operational projections provide a foundation for system design but do not establish the effectiveness of integrated PPO/CTDE coordination or live autonomous deployment. The proposed fairness target of DPR ≤ 1.05 also requires operational validation. UNIHAA therefore contributes a computational decision-support architecture whose effectiveness, safety, and scalability require prospective evaluation.

radar.title: Single and multi-winner auctions with performance obligation
radar.summary: Auctioning access rights to private providers through competitive tendering has become a central instrument for governments to regulate markets and public services. While efficient in allocating licenses, such auctions may generate monopolistic market structures with adverse effects on consumer welfare. We experimentally evaluate two policy interventions to mitigate these outcomes: introducing post-tender competition and imposing minimum production obligations on winning firms. Our results show that performance obligations substantially improve welfare by raising output and consumer surplus, albeit at the cost of reduced auction revenue. Extending the design with additional treatments, we demonstrate that genuine competition yields even stronger welfare gains. These findings highlight a trade-off between government revenue and consumer welfare in auction design. We conclude that while obligations are an effective tool to counter monopoly distortions, sustaining competition remains essential to maximise total surplus at the market level.

radar.title: Regret Bounds for Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade: Learning the Best Posted-Price Mechanism
radar.summary: Bilateral trade models the task of intermediating between two strategic agents, a seller and a buyer, willing to trade a good for which they hold private valuations. We study this problem from the perspective of a profit-maximizing broker in a regret minimization framework. At each time step, a new seller and buyer arrive and the broker proposes a trading price to each agent. The trade happens if both agents accept, and the profit of the broker is the difference between the price received from the buyer and the one paid to the seller. At the end of each interaction, the learner only observes whether the trade occurred, and its goal is to achieve sublinear regret relative to the best fixed pair of prices in hindsight. We start by investigating the adversarial version of the problem, where buyer and seller valuations are generated by an adversary. In this setting, we construct a polynomial-time learning algorithm with a $\tilde O(T^{\frac 23})$ regret rate, which is nearly tight even if the valuations are drawn i.i.d. from independent distributions, thus matching the rate for one-sided pricing. Our adversarial algorithm combines a localized estimation procedure with an information-based minimax construction. We then consider valuations drawn i.i.d. from independent distributions satisfying the monotone-hazard-rate (MHR) property and provide a learning algorithm with nearly tight $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ regret. The algorithm combines localized estimation with a stochastic convex bandit routine applied to the negative logarithm of expected profit. Finally, we complement this result by showing a separation between MHR and regular distributions, proving that the minimax regret rate in the latter setting is $\tilde Θ(T^{\frac 35})$. This last result contrasts with the $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ regret bound that can be obtained for one-sided pricing with regular distributions.
radar.summary_short: Bilateral trade models the task of intermediating between two strategic agents, a seller and a buyer, willing to trade a good for which they hold private valuations. We study this problem from the perspective of a profit-maximizing broker in a regret minimization framework.

Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Integrated Ship–Port–VTS Coordination in Smart Maritime Transportation Systems
radar.summary: Smart maritime transportation requires coordinated decisions across ship arrival management, port services, and Vessel Traffic Services (VTSs). This study develops a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework representing three interacting functions: aggregate arrival adjustment, port-service response, and traffic metering. The coordination problem is formulated as a cooperative Markov game with normalized operating states, discrete actions, and a shared reward incorporating delay, traffic-risk exposure, emissions, and control effort. The controller implements shared-state cooperative independent Q-learning, with centralized information and agent-specific action selection. Training comprises 5000 episodes of 40 decision steps, followed by frozen-policy evaluation against cross-state rule-based coordination and local-state heuristic control over 400 Monte Carlo episodes per strategy. Relative to these benchmarks, respectively, cooperative MARL reduces mean normalized delay by 44.8% and 50.9%, traffic-risk exposure by 30.6% and 41.2%, and anchorage queue intensity by 41.6% and 37.9%. Absolute cumulative system loss decreases by 12.7% and 24.6%. The emissions proxy is 5.1% lower than under rule-based coordination and 2.3% higher than under local-state heuristic control. The reported training trajectory stabilizes during its final phase, while demand and stochastic-noise tests show sustained comparative advantages in delay, traffic-risk exposure, and queue intensity within the specified environment. These findings describe one trained policy evaluated in an aggregate simulation using assumed transition coefficients and normalized performance proxies. The study provides a computational basis for integrated ship–port–VTS coordination, with operational application requiring field calibration, explicit safety constraints, and further evaluation across training seeds and learning-based benchmarks.

radar.title: An Analysis of Zero-Sum Game Agent Training Based on Large Language Models and Self-Play Mechanisms
radar.summary: This paper carries out a review of competitive agent training under zero‑sum game settings, analysing persistent drawbacks found in traditional self‑play reinforcement learning, including inflexible decision‑making policies and weak long‑horizon reasoning capacity. Game agents built purely upon large language models are incapable of sustaining iterative upgrades amid ongoing adversarial contests. Accordingly, the present work investigates viable integration schemes that unite large language models and self‑play training systems. It first lays out the definition of zero‑sum games, illustrates standard self‑play training workflows, and revisits fundamental algorithms from game theory. Four practical integration patterns are classified, namely auxiliary policy generation, reward evaluation optimisation, accumulation of adversarial experience, and the construction of diversified training opponents. Relying on theoretical formula derivation and comparative experimental statistics, this paper evaluates widely adopted modern frameworks against five core benchmarks: reasoning performance, training productivity, generalisation capability, computational expenditure, and training stability, so as to compare their distinct strengths and weaknesses. Evaluation findings indicate that each standalone integration paradigm bears intrinsic flaws. Frameworks adopting dynamically‑generated opponents deliver optimal generalisation performance, while optimised reward mechanisms enable the fastest training convergence. Nonetheless, all hybrid training architectures confront common bottlenecks such as LLM hallucination, prohibitive computational overhead, and oscillating gradient signals during model training. This review identifies several high‑potential research directions: dynamic multi‑module collaborative structures, streamlined self‑play workflows, retrieval‑augmented technologies to restrain hallucination, as well as the development of general‑purpose game agents. The outcomes of this analysis can supply theoretical references for future advances in adversarial decision‑making artificial intelligence.

radar.title: Evaluating reinforcement learning approaches for leaderless UAV swarms in obstacle-laden environment
radar.summary: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms provide huge potential for complex missions, yet coordinating large-scale collectives in obstacle-laden environments without a single global leader remains a significant challenge. While Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has become a dominant paradigm for such coordination, systematic comparisons of how different training architectures perform within hierarchical manager-worker swarm topologies that deliberately eliminate the top-level aggregator remain absent from the literature. This study compares centralized (CTDE), decentralized (DTDE), and federated (FTDE) training approaches, all with decentralized execution, for a leaderless hierarchical UAV swarm of 18 agents organized into three manager-worker clusters. All paradigms are implemented using Asynchronous Proximal Policy Optimization (APPO) and evaluated over a fixed ten-session training budget. Centralized learning achieves the highest final reward, while federated learning attains the highest cumulative reward over the training budget by avoiding a mid-training performance drop observed in the centralized approach. Federated learning is also the only approach whose reward stays within a stability band through the end of the training budget, reaches a final collision rate comparable to that of centralized learning, and reduces inter-cluster training communication by approximately 80% relative to centralized learning. Under simulated manager failure, decentralized and federated learning each retain over 94% of nominal performance, compared to 63.9% for centralized learning. A theoretical analysis shows that the inter-cluster communication cost of the federated approach is independent of the number of workers per cluster when the number of manager clusters is fixed, although it grows with the number of clusters. Validation with an alternative algorithm (MAPPO) preserves the ordering of the three approaches on both final and cumulative reward, and an obstacle-density study preserves the final-reward ordering. These results indicate that peer-to-peer federated learning provides a balanced trade-off between learning performance, communication overhead, fault tolerance, and scalability for hierarchical UAV swarms.
radar.summary_short: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms provide huge potential for complex missions, yet coordinating large-scale collectives in obstacle-laden environments without a single global leader remains a significant challenge.

In Which Matching Markets Do Costly Compatibility Inspections Lead to a Deadlock?
radar.summary: A key feature of many real-world matching markets is congestion, i.e., market participants struggle to find match partners. We characterize congestion in a model of random matching markets where an agent pair must perform a mutual inspection to verify compatibility prior to matching with each other. Motivated by the notion of regret-free stability, we assume an agent pair is only willing to {perform a mutual inspection if they are each other's current favorite agent, which guarantees a match if the inspection finds compatibility.} We ask when, in large random two-sided markets, will \emph{information deadlocks} arise in which many agents delay inspections indefinitely awaiting a match guarantee. The market consists of $N$ women and $\alpha N$ men. We characterize the existence and size of information deadlock as a function of the men-to-women ratio $\alpha$, women’s average consideration-set size $K$, and an inspection's success probability $p$, as the number of women $N$ grows. We find a phase transition from a deadlock-free regime (where a vanishingly small fraction of agents are stuck waiting) to the information deadlock regime as $K$ increases, $\alpha$ decreases, or $p$ decreases. Several market-design insights emerge from our characterization. For example, the level of market connectivity $K$ that maximizes the number of matches formed is the level that places the market at the phase boundary between the deadlock-free regime and the deadlock regime. Vertical differentiation between agents reduces deadlock, as does a willingness by agents to {inspect with their top-$k$ current favorites for $k > 1$.} Our analysis is inspired by the machinery of message passing and density evolution from statistical physics, and the emergence of deadlock corresponds to a branching process of preferred partners becoming supercritical.

radar.title: Group size effects and collective misalignment in LLM multi-agent systems
radar.venue_raw: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
radar.summary: Multi-agent systems of large language models (LLMs) are rapidly expanding across domains, introducing dynamics not captured by single-agent evaluations. Yet, existing work has mostly contrasted the behavior of a single agent with that of a collective of fixed size, leaving open a central question: How does group size shape dynamics? Here, we move beyond this dichotomy and systematically explore outcomes across the full range of group sizes. We focus on multi-agent misalignment, building on recent evidence that interacting LLMs playing a simple coordination game can generate collective biases absent in individual models. First, we show that collective bias is a deeper phenomenon than previously assessed: Interaction can amplify individual biases, introduce new ones, or override model-level preferences. Second, we demonstrate that group size affects the dynamics in a nonlinear way, revealing model-dependent dynamical regimes. Finally, we develop a mean-field analytical approach and show that, above a critical population size, simulations converge to deterministic predictions that expose the basins of attraction of competing equilibria. These findings establish group size as a key driver of multi-agent dynamics and highlight the need to consider population-level effects when deploying LLM-based systems at scale.

radar.title: A Better Cycle-Breaker for Direct Democracy?
radar.summary: When a counter-proposal is made to an initiative to change the Swiss constitution, the citizenry makes three binary majority choices: the initiative versus the status quo, the initiative versus the counter-proposal, and the status quo versus the counterproposal as a tie-breaker. If there is a cycle, the alternative that beats the status-quo wins. This system invites strategic voting, as exemplified by the 2010 case of the “Ausschaffungsinitiative”. We suggest to break cycles differently by choosing the middle alternative in case of a cycle, which will normally be the counter-proposal. More precisely, we show that there always exists a strong Nash equilibrium in which all citizens vote sincerely. Moreover, the outcome of all alternative strong equilibria with strategic voting is the same as if everybody votes sincerely. We also show that other common cycle-breaker rules cannot achieve the same result.

radar.title: Sustainable Multi-Zone Greenhouse Fertigation Through Reliability-Aware Sensing, Spatiotemporal Graph Learning, and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
radar.summary: With protected agriculture increasingly developing toward large-scale, multi-zone, and intelligent production, reducing water and fertilizer consumption, drainage losses, and energy waste while maintaining crop yield, product quality, and long-term economic profitability has become an important challenge for sustainable greenhouse production. To address sensor abnormalities, spatial heterogeneity among irrigation zones, competition for shared hydraulic resources, and the limited ability of conventional control strategies to jointly optimize resource efficiency and economic performance, a sensor-driven spatiotemporal graph multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, termed SensorGraph-FertiMARL, is proposed for state sensing, response prediction, and sustainable coordinated fertigation optimization in multi-zone greenhouses. Reliable zone-level states are first obtained through sensor-reliability gating, missing-state reconstruction, and multi-relational graph fusion incorporating spatial, hydraulic, and microclimatic relationships. An action-conditioned fertigation–yield–quality–profit digital twin is then constructed to jointly predict root-zone responses, resource consumption, marketable yield, product quality, and net profit associated with candidate control actions. Finally, graph-based multi-agent proximal policy optimization (Graph-MAPPO) with capacity, safety, and fairness constraints is employed to coordinate fertigation allocation among multiple zones under shared pump, main-pipeline, and nutrient-solution resource constraints. Evaluated through rigorous offline digital-twin simulation and replay testing calibrated against complete multi-stage historical dataset records from an eight-zone commercial greenhouse, experimental results show that the proposed method reduced water and fertilizer use to 75.8% and 78.3% (achieving water and fertilizer saving rates of 24.2% and 21.7%), respectively, relative to the uniform timer-based control baseline, while decreasing the drainage rate to 7.2%. The Grade-A product rate increased to 84.6%, net profit reached 138.9% of the baseline level (a +38.9% net-profit improvement), return on investment (ROI) reached 1.94, and the stress-violation rate was limited to 2.9%. For state sensing and digital-twin prediction, the sensor-state reconstruction mean absolute error (MAE) and coefficient of determination (R2) were 0.036 and 0.918, respectively; the water-content prediction MAE was 0.041, the electrical conductivity (EC) prediction root mean squared error (RMSE) was 0.119, and the drainage prediction mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 8.7%. In addition, the R2 for marketable-yield prediction reached 0.912, the macro-averaged F1 (Macro-F1) score for quality-grade prediction reached 0.851, the R2 for net-profit prediction reached 0.904, the mean prediction interval width (MPIW) was 0.142, and the prediction interval coverage probability (PICP) reached 0.931. These results demonstrate that SensorGraph-FertiMARL can simultaneously achieve water and fertilizer conservation, drainage reduction, operational-risk control, and economic improvement while maintaining marketable production and quality, thereby providing an effective intelligent optimization approach for resource-efficient, environmentally sustainable, and economically viable greenhouse production.

radar.title: Posterior-conditioned multi-agent reinforcement learning for adaptive cyber defense
radar.summary: Cyber defense increasingly relies on teams of autonomous agents that must act under partial observability while adversaries shift tactics and objectives over time. Standard multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) methods often overfit to fixed threat models, whereas worst-case robust training can be overly conservative and fail to use observations about the active attack regime. We propose posterior-conditioned MARL, a context-aware framework formulated as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP). In addition to its local history, each defender conditions its decentralized policy on a shared attack-context belief, a probabilistic representation of the attack regime inferred online from recent multi-agent interaction trajectories. This belief provides a low-dimensional representation of evolving adversarial behavior and enables coordinated adaptation during execution without test-time policy optimization or retraining. We provide a performance analysis that quantifies how errors in the inferred attack-context belief translate into degraded long-term defense performance, clarifying the tradeoff between robustness and adaptivity. Experiments on the Cyber Autonomy Gym for Experimentation (CybORG) CAGE-4 cyber operations testbed show improved mission reward and adaptability, particularly under mixed and switching attack conditions, compared with domain-randomized, worst-case robust, and hierarchical defense baselines.

radar.title: Online LLM Inference Routing for Multi-Agent Systems under Long-Term Budget and Layered Privacy Constraints
radar.summary: Abstract The Cloud-Edge-End (CEE) collaborative architecture has become a key paradigm for deploying highly intelligent multi-agent systems with low latency and high energy efficiency. Existing studies on efficient task offloading in CEE, however, either overlook long-term financial budget constraints from commercial API token usage and edge computing leasing, or inadequately handle layered information-sharing and privacy restrictions in decentralized autonomous agents. This paper investigates online inference routing to minimize the computational and communication overhead of large language model (LLM) workloads under long-term budget constraints, agent intent-sharing limitations, and un-known future prompt lengths. We propose a budget-aware online optimization framework that uses Lyapunov optimization to decouple long-term financial constraints, and show that the decoupled problem forms a generalized ordinal potential game. To address heterogeneous information-sharing restrictions, we design an adaptive best response algorithm for cooperative environments with shared decision information, and a multi-agent distributed routing algorithm for limited-information environments, enabling efficient offloading without inter-agent intent sharing. Theoretical analysis provides conditional performance and queue-length bounds and establishes finite convergence of the per-slot solvers. Simulations on distributed inference testbeds show that our scheme reduces the inference overhead of heterogeneous agentic tasks while achieving a favorable trade-off between performance and actual token expenditure.

radar.title: SELFISH AND COOPERATIVE BEHAVIOUR IN NONATOMIC CONGESTION GAMES
radar.summary: The paper examines the influence of cooperative behavior on the players' population assignment among alternatives in a non-atomic congestion game with affine cost functions. The formulation of the congestion game is proposed in which the player population consists not only of individualists but also of players acting in the interests of a cooperating group. In this formulation, a Nash equilibrium is explicitly obtained, allowing us to analyze the interdependence and interaction of strategies for assigning players among alternatives in a non-atomic congestion game with groups of cooperating players. It is proven that the number of alternatives sought by cooperating players is always no less than the number sought by individualists. Moreover, when groups of cooperating players compete in a congestion game, a larger number of alternatives can only be sought by a larger group. Finally, it is shown that the average payoff of a cooperating player is never greater than the payoff of an individualist.

radar.title: Trading Off Business and Family Investments: Evidence from U.S. Entrepreneurial Households
radar.summary: Investing in children’s human capital reduces business investments for U.S. entrepreneurial households. Using financial account data of 90,000 small businesses linked to their owners and a regression discontinuity design that compares the business performance of households with college-aged dependents (18–22) to those with near-college-aged dependents (14–17), I show that business revenues and expenses decline sharply when owners’ children reach age 18. Despite the declines, profitability and productivity remain largely unaffected, suggesting a general downsizing rather than a loss in efficiency. Heterogeneity analysis shows that downsizing is concentrated among highly indebted owner households and businesses with volatile cash flows. For each dollar increase in household spending associated with a child turning 18, business expenses decline by $2.26. These findings are consistent with entrepreneurial parents reallocating capital from business investments toward their children’s human capital, as both compete for the same pool of internal family financial resources. radar.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration
radar.summary: Discovering cooperative behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is challenging due to the combinatorial complexity of joint state-action spaces, which hinders the emergence of coordinated behaviors from trial-and-error alone. Intrinsic rewards are often used to aid discovery, but naively combining them with team objectives can distort the learning signal, compromising task performance. In this paper, we propose EFXPLORER, a constrained exploration framework that maximizes exploration objectives subject to a constraint that preserves established task performance. We solve the resulting problem using an epigraph reformulation that introduces adaptive exploration budgets. This approach separates intrinsic rewards from task objectives and regulates exploration through task feasibility. To further encourage diverse and temporally extended exploration, we incorporate a successor distance-based intrinsic reward that captures long-horizon dependencies. Empirically, our method outperforms strong baselines and induces novel cooperative strategies across SMAX, VMAS, and MPE benchmark suites.

radar.title: H^2MARL: Hierarchical Heterogeneous Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Humanoid Robot Control
radar.summary: Coordinated whole-body control of humanoid robots remains challenging due to high-dimensional coupled dynamics and substantial physical heterogeneity across joint degrees of freedom (JDoFs). Existing multi-agent reinforcement learning methods either employ coarse agent partitions or directly apply generic heterogeneous-agent algorithms, while hierarchical controllers commonly optimize high-level planning and low-level execution independently, leading to uncoordinated motion. In this paper, we propose H^2MARL, a hierarchical heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework with two key mechanisms. We first formulate humanoid whole-body control using a JDoF-level physical-heterogeneity-aware policy factorization, where each torque-actuated JDoF is conditioned on an explicit descriptor of its actuation, kinematic, and dynamic properties. Moreover, we develop a closed-loop policy-executor co-optimization mechanism that jointly adapts the high-level pose planner and the low-level joint executor using shared interaction trajectories, thereby reducing the distribution mismatch between planning and execution. Extensive experiments in MuJoCo and Isaac Gym demonstrate that H^2MARL consistently improves locomotion stability, gait coordination, and motion quality over homogeneous, coarse-grained, and independently optimized alternatives.

radar.title: Autonomous AI-Driven Security Operations Centers (Autonomous SOC): Agentic Orchestration, Real-Time Incident Response, and Multi-Agent Defensive Playbooks
radar.venue_raw: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
radar.summary: Abstract—Contemporary enterprise Security Operations Centers (SOCs) are on the brink of systemic collapse driven by three converging factors: exponential alert fatigue (>25,000 uninvestigated alerts daily per enterprise), acute global cybersecurity workforce shortages, and the emergence of automated, machine-speed cyber threats executing multi-stage Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) in sub-minute time horizons. Traditional Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platforms rely on brittle, rigid, hard-coded linear playbooks that fail when adversaries deviate slightly from known MITRE ATT&CK patterns. The paradigm of the Autonomous AI-Driven SOC (Autonomous SOC) establishes a transformative architecture that replaces rigid rule engines with specialized collaborative Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) powered by fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). In an Autonomous SOC, decentralized cognitive agents autonomously triage alerts, execute deep forensic graph correlation, synthesize non-linear incident playbooks, isolate compromised endpoints via zero-trust API invocations, and conduct automated counter-adversarial negotiations. However, deploying autonomous agentic execution in mission-critical defensive infrastructure exposes severe risks: catastrophic hallucination loops during remediation, prompt injection propagation across defensive pipelines, decision deadlock, and unauthorized disruption of legitimate enterprise operations. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of Autonomous SOC architectures. We formalize incident response as a decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) under dynamic threat uncertainty, model consensus verification over cryptographic remediation DAGs, and establish a dual-tier human-on-the-loop (HOTL) safety gating mechanism. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise SOC evaluation testbed spanning 10,000 multi-stage attack scenarios across real-world enterprise topologies. Our empirical findings demonstrate that our multi-agent autonomous framework slashes Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) from 18.4 minutes to 4.2 seconds and Mean Time to Remediate (MTTR) from 42.6 minutes to 18.2 seconds (a 99.3% reduction) while preserving a 99.6% remediation accuracy against MITRE ATT&CK kill chains. Finally, we formulate open challenges in adversarial prompt-injection resilience, continuous defensive co-evolution, and liability attribution under international cyber law.

radar.title: Instantiating the Knowledge Plane
radar.summary: In 2003, Clark et al. proposed the "Knowledge Plane", a layer of intelligent agents that share rich information about network state in order to collaboratively manage the Internet across administrative boundaries. The technology of the day lacked the two capabilities it demanded most: reasoning and unstructured communication. Thus, automated network management has remained largely confined to single domains, while interdomain problems are still resolved by human operators on the phone. We argue that agentic large language models can finally unlock the potential of the Knowledge Plane, but that doing so will require solving new research problems that arise particularly in this decentralized, multi-agent, coopetitive setting that have received limited attention in the literature thus far.
